people.gloss: Jade pendants beside the singing bells (Vương Bột: bội ngọc minh loan)
people.role: A founder (960) and head of Minh Loan Các; casts the ward bells of Lạc Hà's ships, caravans and Cloud Bridge
people.appearance: A stout, quick woman with burn-scarred forearms, three blue jade pendants at her throat and a laugh that carries across a market.
people.backstory: Yến Bội Ngọc was born in 910 in Vật Hoa Thị, a bronze-dealer's daughter, and learned refining in the workshops of Thiên Bảo Trai under Phan Vật Hoa (phan_vat_hoa). There she met Hoa Minh Hòa (hoa_minh_hoa), a smith's son from Tử Điện Thành who cut jade. In 960 they cast and carved for their Dao-partner rite: she the luan bell, he the jade pendants. They founded the pavilion on the coast that year (V102) and made ward bells for ships, whose note drives off sea beasts and carries a warning. In the cold winter of 1121 (V100) the great bell Hoa was casting cracked in the pit and killed him (N-minh_loan-02). She has headed the pavilion alone since then. In 1183 Lạc Hà's array master Quách Tiếp Vân (quach_tiep_van) ordered forty bells for the Cloud Bridge (N-lac_ha-04). Her casting master cast them on the shoulder of Tằng Loan Phong, and they rang true there. In 1188 she moved the casting floor and the inner pavilion up the mountain and left the wharf to the ships (N-minh_loan-03).
people.wants: To finish the Hundred-Bell Eaves on the mountain before she dies, and to learn what has been ringing the Cloud Bridge bells from below.
people.secret: Hoa did not want to cast in the frost of 1121. She had promised Lạc Hà its harbour bell by the new year, and she made him pour. The pavilion believes the cold killed him. She made the rule against casting in winter herself, the next spring, so that no one would ask why.

people.role: Elder and casting master on Tằng Loan Phong
people.appearance: A gaunt, silent man the colour of clay, deaf in his left ear from a bell he stood too close to.
people.backstory: A red-earth farmer's son from Xích Thổ Thôn and Hoa Minh Hòa's (hoa_minh_hoa) last disciple. He was at the pit in 1121. He cast Lạc Hà's forty Cloud Bridge bells on the mountain's shoulder in 1183 because the coast's damp made them ring flat, and he talked Yến Bội Ngọc (yen_boi_ngoc) into the move. He strikes every new bell against the Winter Crack and has spent forty years trying to cast his master's unstruck bell in bronze.

people.role: Keeper of the forty bells on Lạc Hà's Cloud Bridge at Vân Kiều Trấn
people.appearance: A small, round-shouldered woman with a hand bell at her belt who tilts her head to listen before she answers anything.
people.backstory: Thẩm Hưởng Nhi was born in 1160 at Lam Ngọc Khoáng, the blue jade mine on the mountain, where her father cut stone for Thiên Bảo Trai. She could hear a crack in a bell before it was struck. Yến Bội Ngọc (yen_boi_ngoc) took her as her last disciple in 1176. In 1184 she hung the forty bells on Quách Tiếp Vân's (quach_tiep_van) Cloud Bridge Array (N-lac_ha-04) and stayed at Vân Kiều Trấn to keep them. She tunes them every dusk and has become friends with the array runner Miêu Thạch Lan (mieu_thach_lan), who tends the galleries under the seat. Since 1191 the bells at the bridge's foot have rung on new-moon nights with no wind. The note is low, and it comes from below. She reported it to her master, who wrote to Quách and told her to say nothing to anyone else.
people.wants: To know what rings the bridge bells from below, and to be allowed to say so.
people.secret: In 1197 she followed the note down to a locked door in the lowest silver gallery. On the new moon she heard someone behind it reading aloud, slowly, in the voice of Lạc Hà's head, and the bells answered every line. She has told no one, not even Miêu Thạch Lan.

people.role: Steward of the Bell Wharf, the pavilion's old seat on the coast
people.appearance: A loud, salt-tanned woman with a captain's ledger in one hand and a bell clapper in the other.
people.backstory: A net-mender's daughter from Tân Khẩu Thôn, the harbour where Vô Định's refugees never speak of the plain (A182). She keeps the Bell Wharf, where ships and caravans are still fitted with ward bells, and she knows every captain on the bay by his bell's note. She refused to go up the mountain in 1188. Her friend Nhạc Hải Âm (nhac_hai_am) sailed on Lạc Hà's island warden Lận Viễn Phàm's (lan_vien_pham) first boat in 1158 and did not come back.

people.role: Co-founder of Minh Loan Các (960); Yến Bội Ngọc's Dao partner
people.backstory: A smith's son from Tử Điện Thành, Lạc Hà's armoury city, who cut jade better than he cast bronze. He met Yến Bội Ngọc (yen_boi_ngoc) in Thiên Bảo Trai's workshops, carved the jade pendants for their rite in 960, and founded the pavilion with her (V102). He believed the best bell is never struck. He died in the pit in the winter of 1121 when Lạc Hà's harbour bell cracked as it cooled (N-minh_loan-02).

ties.note: his last disciple

people.cause: lost at sea aboard Lạc Hà's island warden's first boat, at 108
people.role: Ship-bell ringer; lost looking for Cô Phàm's fleet
people.backstory: A ship-bell ringer who signed on with Lận Viễn Phàm's (lan_vien_pham) first boat in 1158 to ring it past the edge of Cô Phàm's charts; the boat did not come back, and Ông Hải Linh (ong_hai_linh) still listens for its bell.
